C.2 Radial modulation and exact restoration of the radial moment functions.

Lemma C.1 built the loop while keeping psp_s fixed. This subsection inserts that loop into the profiles E,UE,U and controls the resulting change in psp_s, which is determined by their radial moments through (4.16). Evaluate periodic antiderivatives at Nlog⁡XN\log X and divide them by NN. Then the profile values change by O(N−1)O(N^{-1}), while the shear changes by order one. The proof of Proposition C.2 proves these estimates, bounds the resulting moment errors by O(N−1)O(N^{-1}), and removes the errors on the reserved correction interval. The comparison with the fixed input profile E,U,ΠE,U,\Pi in the next proposition does not say that the radial derivatives are small.

Proposition C.2.

Start with the fixed input profile E,U,ΠE,U,\Pi chosen at the beginning of this appendix. A sufficiently large finite integer NN, together with a correction supported in the first reserved patch in the intermediate power-law interval, gives smooth profiles Ẽ,Ũ,Π̃\widetilde E,\widetilde U,\widetilde\Pi with Ẽ>0\widetilde E>0 for X>0X>0. These profiles obey the admissible stress cone everywhere in (Xa,Xb)(X_a,X_b). Both endpoint collars, the rectangle near the axis described above, and the two patches reserved for higher-order and mean corrections stay unchanged. Define 𝔪̃,Q̃s,Ñs\widetilde{\mathfrak m},\widetilde Q_s,\widetilde N_s from these profiles by (4.15) and (4.16). Then

(𝔪̃,Π̃,Q̃s,Ñs)=(𝔪,Π,Qs,Ns)beyond the first correction patch.(\widetilde{\mathfrak m},\widetilde\Pi,\widetilde Q_s,\widetilde N_s) =(\mathfrak m,\Pi,Q_s,N_s) \qquad\text{beyond the first correction patch}. Before that point, the profile values and any fixed number of η\eta-derivatives differ from those of the input profile by O(N−1)O(N^{-1}).

Proof.

The loop has the same prescribed averages as the original shear, so their differences have mean zero in the periodic variable. Let 𝒜,ℬ\mathscr A,\mathscr B be the unique zero-mean periodic antiderivatives

∂φ𝒜=−12(aL−a),∂φℬ=12E(bL−bs).\begin{equation} \partial_\varphi\mathscr A=-\tfrac12(a_L-a), \qquad \partial_\varphi\mathscr B=\tfrac12E(b_L-b_s). \tag{C.11} \end{equation}(C.11) They exist because of (C.1), are smooth, and are identically zero on the boundary neighborhoods of ℐ\mathcal I. Extend them by zero in the radial direction and set

EN=Eexp⁡(𝒜(X,η,Nlog⁡X)N),UN=U+ℬ(X,η,Nlog⁡X)N.\begin{equation} E_N=E\exp\!\left(\frac{\mathscr A(X,\eta,N\log X)}{N}\right), \qquad U_N=U+\frac{\mathscr B(X,\eta,N\log X)}{N}. \tag{C.12} \end{equation}(C.12) This extension joins smoothly to the input profiles E,UE,U. In the next identity, 𝒟X=X∂X\mathcal D_X=X\partial_X differentiates a function of (X,η,φ)(X,\eta,\varphi) while φ\varphi is held fixed. Every resulting term is then evaluated at φ=Nlog⁡X\varphi=N\log X. The exact shears of (C.12) are

aN=aL−2𝒟X𝒜N,bN=e−𝒜/N(bL+2𝒟XℬNE).\begin{equation} a_N=a_L-\frac{2\mathcal D_X\mathscr A}{N}, \qquad b_N=e^{-\mathscr A/N}\left(b_L+\frac{2\mathcal D_X\mathscr B}{NE}\right). \tag{C.13} \end{equation}(C.13) After the substitution, X∂XX\partial_X becomes 𝒟X+N∂φ\mathcal D_X+N\partial_\varphi. Insert (C.11) into aN=1−2X∂Xlog⁡ENa_N=1-2X\partial_X\log E_N and bN=2X∂XUN/ENb_N=2X\partial_XU_N/E_N. This gives both formulas, including the exponential denominator in the axial shear.

On the fixed compact radial range from X−X_- through the first correction interval, X,E,H,LX,E,H,L all have positive lower bounds. For each fixed m≥0m\geq 0, the phase in (C.12) does not depend on η\eta, so

supX∑j=0m(|∂ηj(EN−E)|+|∂ηj(UN−U)|)≤CmN−1.\begin{equation} \sup_X\sum_{j=0}^m \left(\left|\partial_\eta^j(E_N-E)\right| +\left|\partial_\eta^j(U_N-U)\right|\right) \leq C_mN^{-1}. \tag{C.14} \end{equation}(C.14) The differences between the shears in (C.13) and their loop values obey the same estimate. The derivative X∂X(EN−E)X\partial_X(E_N-E) can still have order one. More generally, for fixed r≥1r\geq 1 and m≥0m\geq 0, radially differentiating (C.12) gives the bound Cr,mNr−1C_{r,m}N^{r-1} for the mixed derivatives of the profile difference. Checking the cone condition for the modified profiles also requires control of psp_s, not only of the shear. Its radial integral formulas use profile values and parameter derivatives. The estimates just proved are therefore enough, even though the radial derivatives do not have to be small.

Let 𝔪=(M,I,J,S,Cp)\mathfrak m=(M,I,J,S,C_p) and 𝔪N\mathfrak m_N be the five radial moment functions in (4.15) for E,UE,U and EN,UNE_N,U_N, respectively. Keep the same pressure value Π0(η)\Pi_0(\eta) at the axis, so that ΠN=Π0+Cp,N\Pi_N=\Pi_0+C_{p,N}. Integrate (C.14) across this fixed radial range. The weights in the radial moment definitions are bounded there, so the result is

supX∑j=0m|∂ηj(𝔪N−𝔪)|+supX∑j=0m|∂ηj(ΠN−Π)|≤CmN−1.\begin{equation} \sup_X\sum_{j=0}^m\left|\partial_\eta^j(\mathfrak m_N-\mathfrak m)\right| +\sup_X\sum_{j=0}^m\left|\partial_\eta^j(\Pi_N-\Pi)\right| \leq C_mN^{-1}. \tag{C.15} \end{equation}(C.15) The formulas for Qs,NsQ_s,N_s in (4.16) use these radial moment functions and their first parameter derivatives, together with the profile values. Their denominators stay bounded away from zero on this range. Therefore

supX∑j=0m|∂ηj(ps,N−ps)|≤CmN−1.\begin{equation} \sup_X\sum_{j=0}^m\left|\partial_\eta^j(p_{s,N}-p_s)\right| \leq C_mN^{-1}. \tag{C.16} \end{equation}(C.16) The estimate at order mm uses the profile and radial moment estimates through order m+1m+1 in η\eta. It does not compare radial derivatives. Lemma C.1 gives uniform positive lower bounds in the cone inequalities. Equations (C.13) and (C.16) then preserve the admissible stress cone on ℐ\mathcal I once NN is large enough. Between ℐ\mathcal I and the first correction interval, the fields are still E,UE,U, while ps,N−psp_{s,N}-p_s obeys (C.16). The uniform positive lower bounds in the input profile’s admissible stress cone inequalities therefore remain positive there as well.

The modified profiles now obey the cone inequalities all the way through the joining interval. Their moments still have errors of order N−1N^{-1}, and those errors must be removed before the profile reaches the exterior. Make the correction on the first patch listed after (A.9). This patch comes before the terminal compensation patch and the two later correction patches. On it, the input profiles obey U=0U=0 and E=K(η)X−1/2−λE=K(\eta)X^{-1/2-\lambda}, where KK is smooth and has a positive lower bound. Add two fixed compact bumps to UU and three to EE, with coefficients that depend smoothly on η\eta. List the five radial moment functions at the patch’s right endpoint in the order (M,J;I,S,Cp)(M,J;I,S,C_p). When all coefficients are zero, their differential separates into two independent blocks at first order, with the following weights.

rowsweights in dXpowers of XM,J1,H0,−λI,S,Cp2X,−E,E/X1/2,−1/2−λ,−3/2−λ.\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{rows} & \text{weights in }dX & \text{powers of }X\\ \hline M,J & 1,H & 0,-\lambda\\ I,S,C_p & \sqrt{2X},-E,E/X & 1/2,-1/2-\lambda,-3/2-\lambda. \end{array} The exponents are distinct because λ>0\lambda>0 has already been fixed. Choose bumps with ordered, disjoint supports inside each block. Lemma A.1, or its five-moment specialization in Corollary A.3, then gives an invertible matrix whose inverse is uniformly bounded on [−1,1][-1,1]. That bound may depend on λ\lambda and on the fixed patch scales. The two UU-weights merge as λ→0\lambda\to 0, so no uniform bound in that limit is claimed.

The map from the correction coefficients to the changes in (M,J,I,S,Cp)(M,J,I,S,C_p) is this linear map plus quadratic terms. The function JJ contains the product of the two field changes, while S,CpS,C_p contain their squares. By (C.15), the discrepancy accumulated before this correction is Om(N−1)O_m(N^{-1}). Lemma A.2 therefore gives a smooth solution for coefficients near zero that cancels the discrepancy. For every fixed parameter order, these coefficients are Om(N−1)O_m(N^{-1}). Choose NN after λ\lambda, the patch scales, and every choice used in the fixed input profile. Choose it large enough that the discrepancy lies in the neighborhood where the solution is defined and that its derivatives through the finitely many η\eta-orders needed for positivity and the cone inequalities meet their tolerances. Differentiating the implicit equation gives finite bounds for every further fixed η\eta-derivative order. The derivatives do not all have to be small at once. The fixed bump shapes also keep the correction small in the radial derivatives used by the shear.

Integration gives the correction’s partial radial moment functions the same Om(N−1)O_m(N^{-1}) bounds. Equation (C.16) therefore remains valid inside the correction interval, and the admissible stress cone remains valid throughout that interval.

At the correction interval’s right endpoint, XrepX_{\mathrm{rep}}, the corrected profiles obey

𝔪̃(Xrep,η)=𝔪(Xrep,η),(Ẽ,Ũ)=(E,U)for X≥Xrep.\begin{equation} \widetilde{\mathfrak m}(X_{\mathrm{rep}},\eta) =\mathfrak m(X_{\mathrm{rep}},\eta), \qquad (\widetilde E,\widetilde U)=(E,U) \quad\text{for }X\geq X_{\mathrm{rep}}. \tag{C.17} \end{equation}(C.17) From this endpoint onward, equality of the five radial moment functions continues by integration. Lemma 4.4 then gives equality of the complete pressure and the functions Qs,NsQ_s,N_s for every X≥XrepX\geq X_{\mathrm{rep}}, including equality of their parameter derivatives. This keeps the terminal compensation already built into the input moment vector 𝔪\mathfrak m. As a result, the exterior moments and the pressure normalized to vanish at radial infinity are unchanged. The first collar is unchanged because both modifications are supported later, and the pressure is integrated from the unchanged axis datum. The last collar is unchanged because the radial moments have been restored exactly. The two unused correction patches still have their prescribed reference power law and U=0U=0.

Finally, fix one such finite NN. Every mixed radial and parameter derivative of the resulting profiles is finite, though its bound may depend on this NN. Fix this value before taking any limit in the physical scale qq, and before choosing any later dyadic band or correction stage. ◻

C.3 The two edges and the completed profile.

In this subsection, E,U,ΠE,U,\Pi mean the corrected profiles from Proposition C.2, and every related quantity is formed from those corrected profiles. Proposition C.2 has now supplied the interior cone inequalities and the exact radial moments. It remains to prove Proposition C.3 by checking the remaining assertions at the annular edges, where the stress 𝒯0\mathcal T_0 vanishes. Its direction nn must extend smoothly, and the cone inequalities must keep a strict uniform margin. The derivatives of 𝒯0\mathcal T_0 must also obey the same exponential weight ζ\zeta required in Theorem 4.6. Both endpoint collars were left unchanged, so their original stress factorizations (B.30) and Equations (A.48) to (A.49) give these properties. In the weight below, t1>0t_1>0 is the fixed activation width in log⁡(X/Xa)\log(X/X_a) from Proposition 4.10.

Proposition C.3.

The profiles from Proposition C.2 have every property stated in Theorem 4.6, with the weight

ya=log⁡(X/Xa),yb=log⁡(Xb/X),δ=min⁡{1,ya,yb},ζ=exp⁡(−t12ya2−4yb2)(Xa<X<Xb),\begin{equation} \begin{gathered} y_a=\log(X/X_a), \qquad y_b=\log(X_b/X), \qquad \delta=\min\{1,y_a,y_b\},\\ \zeta=\exp\!\left(-\frac{t_1^2}{y_a^2}-\frac{4}{y_b^2}\right) \qquad (X_a<X<X_b), \end{gathered} \tag{C.18} \end{equation}(C.18) and this weight is extended by zero when X≤XaX\leq X_a or X≥XbX\geq X_b.

Proof.

The stress is zero up to XaX_a because of the analytic axis profile and Proposition B.5. It is zero beyond XbX_b because of Lemma A.8. Proposition C.2 leaves both regions unchanged and makes the admissible stress cone inequalities hold everywhere between them. If the stress were zero at an interior point, the identity (4.11) would force ps=(a,−bs)p_s=(a,-b_s), and hence Pc=vsP_{\mathrm c}=v_s. That contradicts the strict quadratic cone test. This proves the stress-support assertion in part (ii) of Theorem 4.6. The unchanged axis profile also obeys (4.13) when X≤XaX\leq X_a.

For the cone assertions in part (iii), set n=𝒯0/|𝒯0|n=\mathcal T_0/|\mathcal T_0| on Xa<X<XbX_a<X<X_b. The interior bounds F>0F>0, a>0a>0, and vs>2v_s>2 come from the positive profile construction and the admissible stress cone. At the inner endpoint, a=p1,r>0a=p_{1,\mathrm r}>0. Proposition B.5 gives vs>2+cv_s>2+c there, and the analytic axis profile has F>0F>0. At the outer endpoint, the same bounds follow from (A.56), together with bs=0b_s=0 and positivity of the heat factor. Continuity on the compact closed annulus gives the required positive lower bounds throughout the annulus.

The inner edge keeps the factorization 𝒯0=eaB0\mathcal T_0=e_aB_0 from (B.30), where ea=e−t12/ya2ga(ya)e_a=e^{-t_1^2/y_a^2}g_a(y_a), ga(0)>0g_a(0)>0, and B0(0,η)=Fps,r≠0B_0(0,\eta)=Fp_{s,\mathrm r}\neq 0. These facts make its direction smooth.

At the edge, that direction is a positive scalar multiple of the limiting shear (a,−bs)=a(1,ts)(a,-b_s)=a(1,t_s). In particular, nz−tsnθ=0n_z-t_sn_\theta=0 and nθ+tsnz>0n_\theta+t_sn_z>0 there. At the outer edge, the unchanged factors from Proposition A.10 give

n=(bθ,yb6bz)bθ2+yb12bz2,bθ(0,η)>0.n=\frac{(b_\theta,y_b^6b_z)} {\sqrt{b_\theta^2+y_b^{12}b_z^2}}, \qquad b_\theta(0,\eta)>0. The outer limiting direction is therefore (1,0)(1,0), and the limiting shear ratio is ts=0t_s=0. Every statement here remains smooth through η=±1\eta=\pm 1; the heat factor is used only where its argument is nonnegative.

These edge limits make the interior cone inequalities uniform on the closed annulus. In the interior, (4.11) gives

nθ+tsnz=Pc−vs|ps−(a,−bs)|>0,nz−tsnθ=Jc|ps−(a,−bs)|.n_\theta+t_sn_z =\frac{P_{\mathrm c}-v_s}{|p_s-(a,-b_s)|}>0, \qquad n_z-t_sn_\theta =\frac{J_{\mathrm c}}{|p_s-(a,-b_s)|}. The admissible stress cone makes 2−(vs−2)(nz−tsnθ)2/(nθ+tsnz)22-(v_s-2)(n_z-t_sn_\theta)^2/(n_\theta+t_sn_z)^2 positive in the interior. This expression and its positive denominator both extend continuously to the two edges. The factorizations just proved make the expression equal to two at either edge. The expression and the denominator each have a positive minimum on the compact annulus. Those two minima give one 0<κ<20<\kappa<2 for which

nθ+tsnz≥κ,(vs−2)(nz−tsnθ)2≤(2−κ)(nθ+tsnz)2.n_\theta+t_sn_z\geq\kappa, \qquad (v_s-2)(n_z-t_sn_\theta)^2 \leq(2-\kappa)(n_\theta+t_sn_z)^2. These bounds, together with the endpoint directions and the positive lower bounds above, prove part (iii) of Theorem 4.6.

For part (iv), only the following weighted estimates remain to be proved.

|𝒯0|≥cζ,|∂I𝒯0|≤CIζδ−mI(Xa<X<Xb,−1≤η≤1)\begin{equation} |\mathcal T_0|\geq c\zeta, \qquad |\partial^I\mathcal T_0|\leq C_I\zeta\delta^{-m_I} \qquad (X_a<X<X_b,\ -1\leq\eta\leq1) \tag{C.19} \end{equation}(C.19) They must hold for every fixed mixed profile derivative ∂I\partial^I, with finite constants that do not depend on the physical qq.

On an inner collar, ζ\zeta differs from e−t12/ya2e^{-t_1^2/y_a^2} only by a smooth positive factor bounded above and below. The bounds in (B.31) therefore give (C.19) there. On an outer collar, it differs from e−4/yb2e^{-4/y_b^2} in the same way. The angular factor e−4/yb2yb−3bθe^{-4/y_b^2}y_b^{-3}b_\theta, with bθb_\theta bounded below, gives the lower bound, while (A.51) gives the upper bound for every fixed derivative. On the compact interval left between the two collars, both ζ\zeta and |𝒯0||\mathcal T_0| have positive minima, and every fixed derivative is bounded. Putting these three regions together proves (C.19). The exponential factors also show that setting the stress equal to zero across both edges gives a smooth extension. The definition (C.18) makes ζ\zeta positive in the interior and flat at both edges. This completes part (iv) of Theorem 4.6.

For the regularity in part (i), Proposition B.2 gives the smooth axis profiles with F>0F>0, and Corollary B.6 keeps the common analytic rectangle [0,Xan]×[−1,1][0,X_{\mathrm{an}}]\times[-1,1]. The factors give Cartesian smoothness across the axis through Equations (4.4) to (4.5). The later modifications in Proposition C.2 are smooth and preserve positivity, with finite mixed derivative bounds on every fixed radial interval. The inner directional margin is part (iii), proved above. The heat profile is smooth through η=±1\eta=\pm 1 by Lemma A.6; its factor does not need to be analytic at zero. The pressure normalization (4.25) comes from Lemma A.5 and Propositions A.7 and B.8, and (C.17) keeps it unchanged. This completes part (i). Differentiating the pressure formula gives ΠX=E2/(2X)=F2\Pi_X=E^2/(2X)=F^2, including its smooth extension at X=0X=0. Proposition 4.2 gives the exact tangential residual identities. Together with the support and axis checks above, they complete part (ii).

For part (v), Propositions A.7 and B.8 give the exact exterior moments (4.28), and (C.17) keeps them unchanged. The same restoration keeps the heat exterior (4.29); Lemma A.6 proves its exact heat evolution and smoothness. For the radius in this assertion, take Xv=Xend∈(Xa,Xb)X_{\mathrm v}=X_{\mathrm{end}}\in(X_a,X_b),

the pulse-end radius defined before (A.10). Beyond it, U=M=0U=M=0 by Proposition A.4 and (C.17). Therefore 𝒜X(U)=M/X=0\mathcal A_X(U)=M/X=0, and (4.7) gives V0=0V_0=0. This proves the remaining assertion in part (v).

Finally, the third and fourth reserved intervals listed after (A.9) are exactly the intervals ℐpos,ℐmean\mathcal I_{\mathrm{pos}}, \mathcal I_{\mathrm{mean}} in part (vi). Both lie in (Xa,Xv)(X_a,X_{\mathrm v}), and their order in the list means that sup⁡ℐpos<inf⁡ℐmean\sup\mathcal I_{\mathrm{pos}}<\inf\mathcal I_{\mathrm{mean}}. Proposition C.2 leaves both intervals unchanged. On them, the input profiles obey U=0U=0 and E=K(η)X−1/2−λE=K(\eta)X^{-1/2-\lambda}, where K(η)=cpatch(1+η2)−1K(\eta)=c_{\mathrm{patch}}(1+\eta^2)^{-1} for a fixed positive constant cpatchc_{\mathrm{patch}}, by Proposition A.4. They therefore still satisfy (4.30), which completes part (vi). Proposition C.2 fixed the finite frequency NN before choosing the physical scale qq and every later band and correction stage. The constants therefore have the independence stated at the end of Theorem 4.6. ◻
